item.title: How to Build a Hardware Brand in Nigeria: SOLA Dealer Success Stories
item.description:
How to Build a Hardware Brand in Nigeria: SOLA Dealer Success Stories

Want to go from “just another importer” to a trusted hardware brand in Nigeria? It’s possible — and we’ve seen it happen many times.

SOLA Hardware works with over 100 dealers across Nigeria, and we’ve studied what makes the top 20% successful. This guide shares their strategies — plus real success stories from Lagos, Abuja, and Port Harcourt.

item.title: Nigeria Hardware Import: Payment Methods & Logistics Complete Guide 2026
item.description:
Nigeria Hardware Import: Payment Methods & Logistics Complete Guide 2026

Importing door hardware from China to Nigeria can be highly profitable — but only if you master the payment and logistics details. As a supplier with 10+ years exporting to Nigeria, SOLA Hardware has seen every mistake and every success story.

This guide covers everything from payment security to shipping options, SONCAP certification, and how to avoid scams.

📋 Table of Contents

  1. Payment Methods: What’s Safe in 2026?
  2. Shipping Options: LCL vs FCL vs Air Freight

  6. SOLA Hardware’s Nigeria Support Package

The Big 5 Payment Methods

item.title: Certifications That Matter (And Ones That Don't) — From 10 Years of Nigerian Customs Nightmares
item.description:
Certifications That Matter (And Ones That Don’t) — From 10 Years of Nigerian Customs Nightmares

Let me start with 2018. A new customer ordered a container of locks and paid extra for “CE certification.” The supplier sent a nice PDF certificate, and off we went.

The container got to Lagos — and sat there for 3 weeks. Why? The CE certificate was fake. The customer had to pay $4,500 in fines and demurrage, then had to fly to Lagos to fix it.

item.title: Door Handle Materials Guide: What Actually Sells in Nigeria (From 10 Years of Experience)
item.description:
Door Handle Materials Guide: What Actually Sells in Nigeria (From 10 Years of Experience)

Let me start with a story from 2019, when I made a costly mistake. A new customer from Port Harcourt ordered 2,000 SS201 handles for a beachfront estate project. I warned him SS201 would rust, but he said “it looks the same and saves money.”

Six months later, he was back — all 2,000 handles had rust spots. He lost the trust of his client, and I lost a good customer.

item.title: How to Import Door Hardware from China Without Losing Your Shirt — 10 Years of Mistakes I've Seen
item.description:
How to Import Door Hardware from China Without Losing Your Shirt — 10 Years of Mistakes I’ve Seen

Let me start with a story from 2017. A new Nigerian customer ordered a 20GP container of locks from a “cheap” supplier he found on Alibaba. The price was 20% lower than ours, and he thought he got a great deal.

When the container arrived in Lagos, the locks were garbage. They fell apart when you used them, and the finish peeled off. He couldn’t sell them. He lost $12,000 and almost quit the hardware business.

item.title: Nigeria Hardware Market 2026 — What I've Learned After 10 Years of Selling There
item.description:
Nigeria Hardware Market 2026 — What I’ve Learned After 10 Years of Selling There

Let me start with a number: 527. That’s how many Nigerian customers we’ve worked with since 2016. Some ordered once and disappeared. Some have ordered every 3 months for 8 years.

This guide isn’t about “market projections” from a textbook. It’s about what I’ve learned after 10 years of WhatsApp calls at 2 a.m., containers stuck in Lagos ports, and customers who became friends.

item.title: What Door Locks Actually Sell in Nigeria (10 Years of Sales Data)
item.description:
What Door Locks Actually Sell in Nigeria (10 Years of Sales Data)

Let me show you something — here’s our actual sales breakdown from 2025:

Lock Type Percentage of Sales
Mortise Locks 45%
Padlocks 35%
Cylinder Locks 10%
Smart Locks 6%
Everything Else 4%

That’s right — mortise locks and padlocks make up 80% of our sales. Smart locks are growing, but they’re still a tiny part of the market.

item.title: What Door Handles Actually Sell in Nigeria (And What Doesn't) — 10 Years of Experience
item.description:
What Door Handles Actually Sell in Nigeria (And What Doesn’t) — 10 Years of Experience

Let me show you our top 3 finishes from 2025:

Finish Percentage of Sales
Satin Nickel 60%
Polished Chrome 25%
Matte Black 15%

That’s right — satin nickel alone makes up 60% of our sales. Fancy finishes like antique bronze? They look nice, but they just don’t sell.

This guide isn’t about “the perfect door handle” — it’s about what actually sells in Nigeria, based on 10 years of orders from 500+ customers.
